fichas.title: Supporting slopes in loose ground
fichas.summary: Biological engineering can integrate slope support into the vegetative scene. Steep slopes should ideally transition to flatter terrain and be planted with grass, perennials, or trees. Support methods shown or described include turf, fascines, paving, masonry, anchors, rock bolts, shotcrete, and anchored beam grillages. Large cuttings may require staged excavation and immediate support.
uses: Stabilize steep slopes and loose ground
Integrate engineered slopes into the landscape

fichas.title: Rock slopes and revetment
fichas.summary: Rock slope form is determined by geology and jointing. The sheet illustrates rock cladding or masonry revetment, walls built in front of rock or bonded directly to it, and slope designs for strata of variable stability. Steep artificial slopes require special retention measures; unstable or non-solid strata may require flattening or retention.
fichas.building_type: Rock slope protection and retaining structures
uses: Protect rock faces with revetment or masonry
Adapt slope support to geology and strata stability

fichas.title: Krainer wall and Ebensee system
fichas.summary: A spatial-grid retaining wall (Krainer wall) is shown, including stepped installation and an Ebensee system component table. The stepped wall can provide room for a new road while retaining a green landscape. The table lists component lengths, widths, heights, and weights per unit.
uses: Provide space for a new road
